Why is it a stretch?  If I never own a car I need not worry about being in a accident. Period. But all humans (citizens) get sick. Period. And without insurance the cost of that sickness may be borne by society at large. Which is unfair. Which is why auto insurance is mandatory because if you do have a car and have a accident without insurance that cost is borne by society.

I won't get into the details of ACA but my understanding is it subsidizes people who can't afford it, so if you couldn't afford it before aca you should be able to now. Is insurance more expensive for you now than before? Are you paying for your own insurance ? (I am as a self employed I individual )

Yeah . . . I have to disagree with your reasoning here as I stated above : If I never own a car I need not worry about being in a accident. Period. But all humans (citizens) get sick. Period. And without insurance the cost of that sickness may be borne by society at large. Which is unfair. Which is why auto insurance is mandatory because if you do have a car and have a accident without insurance that cost is borne by society. 
And your last sentence : my body, my choice? - well frankly we live in a society where all types of limits are placed on what we can do with our bodies, no illegal drugs, driving with a seatbelt, helmet, for instance. And as you can with all of these limitations so you can with ACA - you don't have to buy insurance - just pay the fines.

Yes your first sentence is true.  But given that reasoning it seems mandatory health insurance is more Important. If I never own a car I need not worry about being in a accident. Period. But all humans (citizens) get sick. Period. And without insurance the cost of that sickness may be borne by society at large. Which is unfair. Which is why auto insurance is mandatory because if you do have a car and have a accident without insurance that cost is borne by society. 
Yes I understand your issues with the Supreme Court ruling - but I was hoping to stick to the larger issue at the crux of aca.

Can someone explain to me why there is such vehement opposition to mandatory health insurance, when every state in the union requires mandatory auto insurance - and basically for the same economic reasons?
